official.description_text:
Researcher in simulations of heat-transfer
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health
Job description
The position is located at the division of process technology at KTH and will aim at contributing with simulation of sustainable processes for industry. The present post-doctoral project focuses on CFD simulations of heat-transfer. We consider the flows, turbulence, mixing, and heat-transfer in the simulations. We use high-fidelity simulations to capture the details of the chemical reaction inside complex flows. The work consists of simulation using super-computers, code modification/implementation of new models, data analysis and presentation of the result. The data analysis might include some coding in python for creating/modifying short scripts for using Machine -Learning or modal analysis techniques.
Qualifications
Requirements
Completed doctoral degree or foreign degree deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree in thermal science, fluid mechanics, chemical engineering or energy engineering.
Documented experience (peer reviewed articles in top scientific journals) of CFD simulations with COMSOL with a focus on heat-transfer simulations.
Preferred qualifications
Work independently and motivate to reach the goal.
Ability to collaborate in a multicultural environment.
Use of modal analysis or Machine Learning for data analysis•
Documented experience in implementing new models in CFD codes
Knowledge of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge (Max 1 page long).
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max one pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to 12 months, with access according to agreement.

ai.summary: Post-doctoral CFD simulation position at KTH focused on heat-transfer modelling in sustainable industrial processes. Core work involves high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics, code implementation, and data analysis using supercomputers and Python scripting for machine learning and modal analysis.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position is entirely computational engineering focused (CFD, thermal science, fluid mechanics). No human-centred research, immersive systems, spatial cognition, learning design, or user evaluation. No alignment with target identity of human-centred XR/HCI research.

methodological_fit.rationale: While both domains use data analysis and Python, the methodological approaches diverge fundamentally. Position requires CFD domain expertise, supercomputer simulation fluency, and thermal/fluid physics modelling. Researcher's methods are experimental design, user studies, and qualitative/quantitative evaluation of human interaction. No methodological transfer.

growth_value.rationale: Position would develop Python and machine-learning data analysis skills, but at significant opportunity cost. These are tangential to core growth gaps (advanced statistics, mixed-effects modelling, broader immersive-systems evaluation). Does not advance spatial cognition, HCI methodology, or collaborative systems research.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong institution (positive), and Sweden is in preferred geography (positive). However, this is a post-doc in chemical engineering, not a PhD pathway position. Does not advance candidacy for doctoral programmes in HCI/XR or build networks in immersive systems research. Limited strategic value toward stated target identity and institutions (Aalto, TU Delft).

eligibility_flags: Requires completed doctoral degree; researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress). Ineligible until PhD completion.
Degree must be in thermal science, fluid mechanics, chemical engineering, or energy engineering. Researcher's MSc is in multimedia/XR. Equivalency assessment uncertain.

Requires peer-reviewed publications in top journals on CFD heat-transfer. Researcher has 1 first-author journal article (domain unknown) and a systematic mapping review in progress. Does not meet documented CFD publication requirement.
risks: Fundamental domain mismatch: CFD/thermal engineering versus human-centred XR research. Switching domains would delay PhD candidacy in target field.
No pathway to target institutions or HCI/immersive systems research community.
Position is 12-month fixed-term post-doc, not a doctoral or PhD-pathway role. Does not align with target position types.
Ineligible until PhD is completed; researcher is in thesis stage.
Risk of career drift: Accepting this position signals pivot away from stated target identity.
